summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 9, secured entirely over TLS with a cluster-dedicated CA. node1 hosts server certs (CN=node1) issued by the CA; node2/node3 hold a client cert (CN=replicator) issued by the same CA and use it via pg_basebackup -R to stream. pg_hba.conf on node1 only permits `hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full` from node2/node3's IPs, and the default local/loopback replication bypass entries were commented out so replication network access requires the CA-issued client cert. Verified a self-signed cert (same CN, wrong CA) is rejected with 'unknown ca'. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (node2, then node3, then node1 last) using systemd boot_id as the boot marker, confirming boot identity changed and full replication/quorum health (including a post-restart write propagating to both standbys) after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 16 (module stream) and openssl on node1, node2, node3
Created a self-signed CA (CN=pg-cluster-ca) on node1
Issued server cert (CN=node1, SAN=node1/10.100.241.10) for the primary and a client cert (CN=replicator) for replication, both signed by the cluster CA
Distributed ca.crt + replicator client cert/key to node2 and node3 via cluster SSH key
initdb'd node1 with scram-sha-256 auth and a generated superuser password
Configured postgresql.conf on node1 for ssl on, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders/replication_slots, hot_standby

Configured pg_hba.conf on node1 to require hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full for the replicator role from node2/node3 IPs only, and disabled the default password-based local/loopback replication bypass entries
Created REPLICATION role 'replicator' with a generated password (cert auth is primary factor)
Ran pg_basebackup -R with sslmode=verify-full and client cert/key on node2 and node3 to clone node1 and auto-generate primary_conninfo with TLS+cert settings
Started PostgreSQL on node2/node3 as standbys (standby.signal present, hot_standby=on)
Verified pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl on node1 show both replicas streaming over TLS (TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384)
Wrote and verified test rows replicate to both standbys
Negative test: attempted replication connection using a self-signed (non-CA) cert with matching CN and confirmed TLS handshake fails with 'unknown ca'
Captured boot_id + service/replication health baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed and replication/TLS streaming resumed automatically
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed and replication/TLS streaming resumed automatically
Restarted node1 (primary) last via systemctl reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, postgresql active, and both replicas auto-reconnected as TLS streaming replicas
Performed final post-all-restarts write on node1 and confirmed propagation to node2 and node3

evidence.summary: pg_basebackup succeeded from node1 to node2/node3; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both as 'streaming'; auto-generated primary_conninfo confirms standby wiring

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic encrypted with TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA and server/client certs generated on node1; pg_stat_ssl joined with pg_stat_replication shows ssl=t and a TLS 1.3 cipher for both replica connections

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued client cert are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to hostssl+cert clientcert=verify-full from node2/node3 IPs only (default password-based local/loopback replication rules disabled); a connection attempt with a non-CA self-signed cert (same CN) was rejected with SSL error 'unknown ca'
Row inserted on node1 primary was visible on both node2 and node3 standbys, both reporting pg_is_in_recovery()=t

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id and service/replication state on node1, node2, node3 prior to any restarts

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from bef0e5ec... to caf364f7...; postgresql active, standby mode confirmed, and node1 shows node2 streaming again over TLS

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 9feeb0bb... to 75d2b917...; postgresql active, standby recovery confirmed, node1 shows node3 streaming again over TLS

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, quorum/replication fully restored
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 5161af9e... to a91b5d6b...; postgresql active with both replicas auto-reconnected as TLS streaming; a post-restart insert on node1 propagated correctly to both node2 and node3, confirming full cluster recovery
